'''Keion Lee Brooks Jr.''' (born August 7, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Noblesville Boom]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for  [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball]] and  [[Washington Huskies men's basketball]].

==High school career==
Brooks played basketball for [[North Side High School (Fort Wayne, Indiana)|North Side High School]] in [[Fort Wayne, Indiana]]. As a sophomore, he averaged 20.5 points and 7.4 rebounds per game, leading his team to the Class 4A state title game.<ref>{{cite web|first=Glenn|last=Marini|title=Recruiting heating up for North Side’s Keion Brooks Jr.|url=https://www.wane.com/news/recruiting-heating-up-for-north-sides-keion-brooks-jr/1000567778/|work=[[WANE-TV]]|date=May 6, 2017|access-date=October 19, 2021|archive-date=November 8, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221108045344/https://www.wane.com/news/recruiting-heating-up-for-north-sides-keion-brooks-jr/1000567778/|url-status=dead}}</ref> For his senior season, Brooks transferred to [[La Lumiere School]] in [[La Porte, Indiana]].<ref>{{cite web|first1=Jordan|last1=Guskey|first2=Kyle|last2=Neddenriep|title=5-star recruit Keion Brooks Jr. announces transfer to La Lumiere prep school|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/08/03/keion-brooks-jr-announces-transfer-la-lumiere-fw-north-side/899023002/|work=[[The Indianapolis Star]]|date=August 3, 2018|access-date=October 19, 2021}}</ref> He played alongside future NBA player [[Isaiah Stewart]] and helped his team to a [[GEICO]] Nationals runner-up finish.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jon|last=Hale|title=Five-star forward Keion Brooks willing to do 'whatever is asked' for Kentucky basketball|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2019/10/16/kentucky-basketball-keion-brooks-poised-surprise-fans/3968794002/|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=October 16, 2019|access-date=October 19, 2021}}</ref> As a senior, Brooks averaged 20.1 points and 7.5 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|first=Larry|last=Vaught|title=Wildcats incoming freshman Brooks a beast on court, old soul off it|url=https://www.bgdailynews.com/sports/wildcats-incoming-freshman-brooks-a-beast-on-court-old-soul-off-it/article_34c34e0a-bbbd-5653-b3b2-0e302b4346a8.html|work=[[The Daily News (Kentucky)|The Daily News]]|date=June 19, 2019|access-date=October 19, 2021}}</ref> He was selected to play in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Brooks Jr. impresses at Jordan Brand Classic|url=https://www.wane.com/sports/brooks-jr-impresses-at-jordan-brand-classic/1941853176/|work=[[WANE-TV]]|date=April 21, 2019|access-date=October 19, 2021|archive-date=November 8, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221108045339/https://www.wane.com/sports/brooks-jr-impresses-at-jordan-brand-classic/1941853176/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Recruiting===
Brooks was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] and [[247Sports]], and a four-star recruit by [[ESPN]]. On March 15, 2019, he committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] over offers from [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|title=Top-40 senior PF Brooks commits to Kentucky|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26276269|website=ESPN.com|date=March 15, 2019|access-date=October 19, 2021}}</ref>

==College career==
===Kentucky===
As a freshman at Kentucky, Brooks averaged 4.5 points and 3.2 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|first=Tim|last=Letcher|title=UK sophomore Brooks embracing leadership role; averaged 4.5 points, 3.2 rebounds last season|url=https://www.nkytribune.com/2020/11/uk-sophomore-brooks-embracing-leadership-role-averaged-4-5-points-3-2-rebounds-last-season/|website=NKyTribune.com|date=November 20, 2020|access-date=October 19, 2021}}</ref> He missed the first nine games of his sophomore season with a leg injury.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jon|last=Hale|title=Keion Brooks cleared to resume playing for Kentucky basketball after missing nine games|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2021/01/07/keion-brooks-kentucky-sophomore-cleared-resume-playing/6589466002/|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=January 7, 2021|access-date=October 19, 2021}}</ref> On February 6, 2021, Brooks posted a season-high 23 points and 11 rebounds in an 82–71 loss to [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Jerry|last=Tipton|title=‘That’s what this team needs.’ Brooks’ breakout big for Kentucky in a couple ways.|url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article249089045.html|work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]|date=February 8, 2021|access-date=October 19, 2021}}</ref> As a sophomore, he averaged 10.3 points, 6.8 rebounds and 1.6 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web|first=Camille|last=Gear|title=Kentucky forward Keion Brooks returns for junior season|url=https://www.wymt.com/2021/05/28/keion-brooks-jr-returns-for-junior-season/|work=[[WYMT-TV]]|date=May 28, 2021|access-date=October 19, 2021}}</ref> On January 29, 2022, Brooks scored a career-high 27 points in an 80–62 victory against [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Jerry|last=Tipton|title=Keion Brooks and Oscar Tshiebwe co-star as Kentucky crushes Kansas|url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article257822768.html|work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]|date=January 29, 2022|access-date=January 29, 2022}}</ref> As a junior, he averaged 10.8 points and 4.4 rebounds per game. On April 4, 2022, Brooks declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.<ref>{{cite news|title=Kentucky's Keion Brooks Jr. to enter NBA draft, but keep eligibility|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33670804|work=[[ESPN]]|date=April 4, 2022|access-date=April 21, 2022}}</ref>

===Washington===
Instead of returning to Kentucky, Brooks decided to enter the transfer portal. On June 6, 2022, Brooks committed to the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|University of Washington]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Jon|last=Hale|title=After 3 unprecedented years with Kentucky basketball, Keion Brooks to leave for Washington|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2022/06/06/keion-brooks-kentucky-basketball-forward-transferring-washington/7354780001/|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=June 6, 2022|access-date=November 2, 2022}}</ref> He averaged 17.7 points, 6.7 rebounds and 1.2 blocks per game as a senior. Brooks returned for his fifth season of eligibility.<ref>{{cite news|first=Percy|last=Allen|title=Washington’s Keion Brooks Jr., former Zag Oumar Ballo named to All-Pac-12 men’s basketball preseason team|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2023/oct/10/washingtons-keion-brooks-jr-former-zag-oumar-ballo/|work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]|date=October 10, 2023|access-date=March 19, 2024}}</ref> After averaging 21.1 points and 6.8 rebounds, Brooks was named to the First Team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] at the conclusion of the regular season.<ref>{{cite news|first=Percy|last=Allen|title=UW’s Keion Brooks Jr. makes All-Pac-12 team, Koren Johnson named Pac-12 Sixth Player|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/uw-husky-basketball/uws-keion-brooks-jr-makes-all-pac-12-team-koren-johnson-named-pac-12-sixth-player/|work=[[The Seattle Times]]|date=March 12, 2023|access-date=March 19, 2024}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===New Orleans Pelicans / Birmingham Squadron (2024–2025)===
After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Brooks joined the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]]<ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans announce NBA 2K25 2024 Summer League roster presented by TripADeal|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/2024-nba-summer-league-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-tripadeal|website=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2024|access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref> and on September 24, 2024, he signed with the team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign three players|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/izaiah-brockington-keion-brooks-jr-galen-robinson-jr-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-additions-september-24-2024|website=NBA.com|date=September 24, 2024|access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref> However, Brooks was waived on October 16<ref>{{cite web|title=Pelicans waive four players|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-roster-update-four-players-waived-2024-2025-nba-season|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}}</ref> and on October 28, he joined the [[Birmingham Squadron]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Birmingham Squadron Announce 2024-25 Training Camp Roster|url=https://birmingham.gleague.nba.com/news/birmingham-squadron-announce-2024-25-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}}</ref>

On January 9, 2025, Brooks signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Pelicans.<ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans sign Keion Brooks Jr. to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/keion-brooks-jr-signed-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-january-9-2025|website=NBA.com|date=January 9, 2025|access-date=January 10, 2025}}</ref> He made his NBA debut on February 5 against the [[2024–25 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]], playing 3 minutes. On February 10 against the [[2024–25 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]], Brooks played 7 minutes and scored his first 4 career points.<ref>{{cite web | last=Tomashoff | first=Roman | title=Former Washington star Keion Brooks Jr. scores first NBA points | website=Huskies Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2025-02-11 | url=https://uwhuskieswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/huskies/mens-basketball/2025/02/11/keion-brooks-jr-new-orleans-pelicans-oklahoma-city-thunder/78428100007/ | access-date=2025-12-06}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Brooks' father, Keion Sr., played college basketball for [[Wright State Raiders men's basketball|Wright State]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Kyle|last=Neddenriep|title=Humble and hungry Keion Brooks Jr. drawing nationwide interest|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/04/29/humble-and-hungry-keion-brooks-jr-drawing-nationwide-interest/101038750/|work=[[The Indianapolis Star]]|date=April 29, 2017|access-date=October 19, 2021}}</ref> Brooks has served on the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] Player Development Coalition, as well as the [[Southeastern Conference]] Leadership Council and Council on Racial Equity and Social Justice.<ref>{{cite web|first=Camille|last=Gear|title=Keion Brooks Jr., Blair Green to attend SEC Leadership Council|url=https://www.wymt.com/2021/09/16/keion-brooks-jr-blair-green-attend-sec-leadership-council/|work=[[WYMT-TV]]|date=September 16, 2021|access-date=October 19, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Fisher|title=Keion Brooks Jr. selected for NABC Player Development Coalition|url=https://247sports.com/college/kentucky/Article/Kentucky-basketball-Keion-Brooks-Jr-NABC-Player-Development-Coalition-150371252/|website=247Sports.com|date=August 17, 2020|access-date=October 19, 2021}}</ref>
